Octahedron counts have explicit vertex and edge-axis transformations and a complete boundary-intersection argument.

Icosahedron: cyclic coordinate permutations and even sign changes act transitively on vertices; the actual five neighbors form a regular pentagon. A 72-degree rotation preserves both antipodal rings and poles. This establishes edge transitivity. One explicit genuine half-turn is transported to every opposite-edge pair, yielding fifteen distinct axes. Odd face/vertex incidences exclude every other case.

Dodecahedron: symmetry transfer through face centers is proved in both directions. All twelve pentagon centers are one positive common scaling of the original icosahedron. The exact scale is justified by the displayed coordinate/radius calculation. No count rests merely on the assertion that the two solids look similar.
For centrally symmetric solids, composing a half-turn with central inversion gives reflection in the perpendicular plane through the center; the converse is also shown.
